title: Duplicate join rows inflate feature configuration beyond parser cap
context: A bot-management control plane produces a binary feature file via a join between rules and permission records. A permissions migration made multiple permission rows visible to a previously narrow database role. The data-plane loader enforces a strict byte-budget. The producer writes one copy per joined row unless DISTINCT is enabled.
semantics: For region r, file_size_kb = header_kb + rules * (1 if distinct else permission_copies) * kb_per_row. A feature-r node fails when file_size_kb > max_file_kb (strictly greater, not greater-or-equal). All values are exact integers. No background retries change the result. Dependent services follow the graph.

hypotheses.description: The US region reaches 128 KB due to a permission duplication.
All feature files fail due to identical rule counts.
APAC exceeds the cap because it has 3 permission copies, regardless of DISTINCT.
The EU file exceeds 100 KB because duplicate permission joins multiply rows without DISTINCT.

actions.meaning: Increase EU loader cap to 150 KB
Increase only the US loader cap
Enable DISTINCT for the EU producer join
Reduce EU permission join multiplicity to one

provenance: Inspired by the 2025-11-18 Cloudflare outage; rule counts, capacity, joins and topology are fabricated.
